title: Nicholls carries bat for 175 as New Zealand make 368; Bumrah takes four
dek: Glenn Phillips completed a century before Akash Deep bowled him, and New Zealand added 125 on the second morning in Wellington. India have begun their reply.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Henry Nicholls carried his bat for an unbeaten 175 and Glenn Phillips completed his second Test century on the second morning at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Friday, as New Zealand were bowled out for 368 in the first Test against India. Jasprit Bumrah finished with four for 92 and Akash Deep with three for 53.

New Zealand resumed on 243 for five and added 125 for their last five wickets. Nicholls and Phillips, who came together at 70 for five on Thursday afternoon, took their sixth-wicket stand to 216 before Akash Deep bowled Phillips for 118 shortly before lunch. New Zealand went to the interval on 317 for six.

## How the morning went

India had the second new ball available from the start of play but could not break the partnership early. Once Phillips fell, the tail went relatively quickly. Prasidh Krishna had Nathan Smith leg before for 14, Akash Deep had Kyle Jamieson caught by KL Rahul for 11, and Bumrah trapped Matt Henry leg before for 1. Nicholls added 20 for the last wicket with Jacob Duffy before Anshul Kamboj had Duffy caught behind by Rishabh Pant for 4.

New Zealand's innings lasted 121 overs. Apart from Nicholls and Phillips, no batter passed 15, and extras, at 20, were the third-highest contribution. The innings swung on one partnership: New Zealand lost five wickets for 70 and five for 82, either side of a stand that was worth more than half their total.

## The bowling

- Jasprit Bumrah: 29-8-92-4
- Akash Deep: 23-7-53-3
- Anshul Kamboj: 23-5-69-2
- Prasidh Krishna: 26-2-100-1
- Washington Sundar: 20-2-45-0

India picked four fast bowlers and Washington Sundar as the only specialist spinner, leaving out Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja. Krishna went for 100 runs in his 26 overs, the most expensive of the attack, while Bumrah again led the way after bowling New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck in the first over of the match.

## India's reply

Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul opened India's innings and had begun cautiously, playing out the first four overs without scoring, according to live scores, when this report was filed. Play on day two is due to end late on Friday morning, Indian time.

## What is at stake

The two-Test series counts towards the 2025-27 World Test Championship, in which New Zealand lead the table and India are fourth. Shubman Gill, India's captain, has said his side need to win five or six of their remaining seven Tests to reach the final. India had New Zealand at 70 for five on the first afternoon, and will now need a total of their own close to 368 to avoid conceding a first-innings lead. The second Test is in Christchurch.
